description: Our goal is to build an interactive web app that transforms NASA Earth observation data into practical, actionable tools for farmers. We already have web development covered, but we are looking for passionate teammates especially data enthusiasts, or team members to help with research and ML agents. Let’s build something impactful together
summary: Since humans learned how to farm, they encounter problems with unpredictable weather and environmental conditions. As technologies improved, we can now easily measure environmental conditions and predict weather more accurately. However, farmers can still have a difficult time interpreting technological terms and numbers. So, we build FarmShift. It will interpret complicated technical NASA satellite DATA into understandable interpretation. Moreover, FarmShift have crop engine that can calculate which crops are best for the location user choose. They can also monitor their plants through NASA satellite real time.
details: FarmShift is a free, mobile-friendly web app that helps farmers in Myanmar decide when to plant in the rice → black gram rotation. A farmer taps their field on a 3D map of Myanmar. The app then pulls NASA POWER weather data for that spot and checks it for heat, warm nights, seasonal rainfall, flooding and rain at harvest. It turns those checks into a simple verdict and a 0–100 score, alongside a recent NASA GIBS satellite photo of the field. Farmers can also map their fields, log farm activities and follow crop health in a 3D view. The app is built with TypeScript, Next.js, React, Three.js, Leaflet and Supabase. It is designed to be clear, honest (it never makes up missing data) and built for Myanmar's own seasons. Connecting real SMAP soil moisture, VIIRS vegetation and GPM rainfall data is the next step. Our goal is to cut lost harvests and help Myanmar farmers adapt to a changing climate.
